The prevalence rate of verotoxogenic Escherichia Coli (VTEC), which is responsible for causing the disease haemorrhagic colitis (HC) and haemolytic uraemic syndrome (HUS), was 6.4 and 21% in slaughtered sheep and goat faeces and in environmental samples, respectively.
VTEC was detected in slaughtered small ruminant animals and environmental samples in Jordan.

VTEC comprised a low percentage of E. coli from small ruminants, slaughterhouses and butcher shops in southern Jordan, and the majority of the isolated VTECs possessed the stx1 and/or stx2 virulent genes, with the stx1 gene being the most common virulence pattern in VTEC.

the characterization of VTEC isolated from slaughtered sheep and goats in southern Jordan.
